description: Frozen acceptance budgets of the A5 tissue material fixtures (tests/vbd/test_vbd_tissue.py). A tolerance is atol + rtol * scale; every entry also records the measured floor it was set from. Most entries here hold on both backends as a single float64-shaped budget: floors measured 2026-09-13 on CPU float64, but loose enough (a locking/discretization/discretization-refinement check, not a tight numeric-parity one) that GPU float32 clears them too. The three entries that did not - axial_force.modulus_ratio, volume_response.interior_position, hollow_tube.rest_kick - are nested by precision, '64' and '32', each measured on its own backend on 2026-09-13; the float64 side is unchanged from before and is never relaxed, only the float32 side is new. Budgets are 1.5 to 2 times the measured floor except where noted (the volume_response section is set far looser than its floor for a documented reason: see its _note). The bending fixture's own docstring records a finding: a force-driven (gravity self-weight) version of the bending test was tried first and gave a tip sag tens of centimetres larger than Euler-Bernoulli theory, essentially unchanged across two decades of Young's modulus - physically impossible for an elastic beam, whose sag must scale as 1/E. That version was abandoned rather than fitted to the observed number; the shape-only, displacement-controlled fixture kept here does not depend on getting a force magnitude right and passes with a small, mesh-resolution-scale error.

axial_force._note: Pins the absolute stiffness scale that the displacement-controlled/shape-only/affine-Dirichlet fixtures above cannot: the axial reaction on the held grip of an extended bar (lx=1.15), read via the solver's own `_kernel_residual_vector` test hook (r_i = -force_i of _func_vertex_system at the settled state), against the closed-form traction P_xx * A0. The two absolute entries carry an identical relative floor because the same ~3.5% offset appears at both E - a systematic Saint-Venant/discretization effect, not noise - while the modulus_ratio entry is what a constant stiffness-scale bug cannot pass: measured to 9.9999997 against an expected 10.0 exactly.

modulus_ratio.unit: dimensionless force ratio vs modulus ratio 10.0

32.note: measured on GPU float32, 2026-09-13; budget is 1.9x the measured floor

volume_response._note: Full-boundary affine Dirichlet data forces the affine field as the unique equilibrium of any convex, homogeneous hyperelastic energy, independent of its specific mu/lam' values: the measured floor here is machine epsilon (~1e-16), not a material-dependent number. This fixture is retained as a no-inversion/no-locking/mass-bookkeeping regression check at a near-incompressible Poisson ratio, not as a quantitative constitutive-law validation - that role is filled by the uniaxial fixtures, whose closed form depends on both mu and lam'. Budgets are set far above the measured floor for exactly this reason.

32.note: measured on GPU float32 at s=0.88 (the tighter of the two dilation parameters, s=1.12 measured 6.05e-8), 2026-09-13; budget is 2.0x the measured floor
measured on GPU float32, 2026-09-13; budget is 2.0x the measured floor
